`readboe` helps R users discover and retrieve official Bank of England
statistical data while retaining the identifiers, raw values, revision fields,
and source receipts needed to reproduce a result. It is intended for analysts,
researchers, and data pipelines that need an explicit contract around official
data and reproducible provenance.

## Coverage at a glance

The bundled discovery snapshot was generated on 3 August 2026. It covers five
related source families:

* **IADB series and revisions:** direct retrieval of known identities, plus
  5,252 validated Bankstats identities across 60 current tables for offline
  discovery. Their series-specific canonical bounds collectively reach from
  June 1969 to July 2026.
* **Bankstats catalogue and bulk workbooks:** 64 current workbook members;
  5,008 catalogue identities have exact current-workbook cells and 244 use
  canonical full IADB history only.
* **Official Bank Rate history and fixed rate identities:** the change history
  begins in October 1694, alongside five fixed daily/monthly/annual Bank Rate
  and SONIA identities whose IADB histories begin in 1975 or 1997.
* **Fitted yield curves:** 11 latest/archive identities across nominal, real,
  inflation, OIS, and discontinued BLC daily/monthly families; nominal monthly
  coverage begins in 1970 and later starts depend on the curve family.
* **Statistical and research release families:** 14 offline registry entries;
  exact asset workflows require the verified snapshot described under
  [Scope and limitations](#scope-and-limitations).

The Bankstats subjects include money and lending, monetary-financial-
institution balance sheets and income, deposits and lending, rates and
exchange rates, public-sector debt and money markets, capital issuance, and
financial derivatives. See [Coverage and source map](data-sources.html#coverage-and-source-map)
for the definitive function/source mapping and snapshot boundaries.

Catalogue and registry discovery are offline-first. Observation and asset
readers use HTTPS connections to allowlisted Bank of England hosts. The package
requires no Bank API key; upstream availability, rate limits, and source terms
still apply.

## Installation

The development version can be installed from GitHub:

```{r install-github, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("chartwell-macro/readboe")
```

The public GitHub repository requires no authentication for installation. No Bank of England API key or login is
collected by the package.

When a released version is accepted by CRAN, the installation will be:

```{r install-cran, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("readboe")
```

## First success: discover an exact series offline

Start with the bundled Bankstats catalogue. This offline call reads the
authenticated snapshot and leaves the managed response cache unchanged.
Searches are case-insensitive implicit-AND matches over the documented identity
and label fields; the returned rows remain in snapshot order.

```{r first-success}
library(readboe)

sonia <- boe_catalogue(query = "SONIA", limit = 1L)
stopifnot(is.data.frame(sonia), nrow(sonia) <= 1L)

sonia[, c(
  "series_id", "displayed_code", "label", "frequency",
  "first_observation", "last_observation", "surface_membership"
)]
```

The identifier in `series_id` is the exact official IADB identity. Keep it in
your own analysis metadata and pass it unchanged to a reader. The result also
has a `boe_catalogue_provenance` attribute describing the snapshot hash, path,
and the number of rows matched before `limit` was applied. The stable fields
can be printed without embedding the installation-specific snapshot path:

```{r catalogue-provenance}
catalogue_provenance <- attr(sonia, "boe_catalogue_provenance")
catalogue_provenance[c("snapshot_sha256", "matched_before_cap", "returned")]
```

For a compact list of well-known policy and benchmark series, use the static
registry. It is also available without network access:

```{r rate-registry}
boe_rate_series()
```

The snapshot is the discovery authority for the Bankstats page represented by
the package. For an identifier documented by another official source, pass
that exact identifier directly; identities outside the snapshot remain outside
catalogue search results.

## Retrieve and chart a time series

This example discovers the official monthly SONIA identity, retrieves a fixed
IADB XML window through `read_boe_series()`, selects the real `date` and
`value` columns, and produces a line chart. Documentation rendering uses an
installed verified replay of the same request, so the article remains fully
offline while exercising the public cache validation and XML parser.

```{r sonia-replay-setup, include=FALSE}
fixture_dir <- system.file(
  "extdata", "sonia",
  package = "readboe", mustWork = TRUE
)
fixture_file <- list.files(
  fixture_dir,
  pattern = "^[0-9a-f]{64}\\.rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
cache_dir <- tempfile("readboe-vignette-cache-")
dir.create(cache_dir)
copied <- file.copy(fixture_file, cache_dir)
stopifnot(length(fixture_file) == 1L, isTRUE(copied))

monthly_sonia <- boe_catalogue(
  query = "SONIA",
  frequency = "Monthly",
  limit = 1L
)
sonia_history <- read_boe_series(
  series_id = monthly_sonia$series_id[[1L]],
  from = "1997-01-31",
  to = "2025-12-31",
  format = "xml",
  cache_only = TRUE,
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
chart_data <- sonia_history$observations[
  !is.na(sonia_history$observations$date) &
    !is.na(sonia_history$observations$value),
  c("date", "value")
]
stopifnot(
  nrow(monthly_sonia) == 1L,
  monthly_sonia$series_id[[1L]] == "IUMASOIA"
)
unlink(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r sonia-data-vignette, eval=FALSE}
monthly_sonia <- boe_catalogue(
  query = "SONIA",
  frequency = "Monthly",
  limit = 1L
)

sonia_history <- read_boe_series(
  series_id = monthly_sonia$series_id[[1L]],
  from = "1997-01-31",
  to = "2025-12-31",
  format = "xml",
  deadline = boe_deadline(30)
)
chart_data <- sonia_history$observations[
  !is.na(sonia_history$observations$date) &
    !is.na(sonia_history$observations$value),
  c("date", "value")
]

monthly_sonia[c("series_id", "label", "frequency")]
utils::head(chart_data, 3L)
```

```{r sonia-chart-vignette, fig.alt="Line chart of 348 monthly average SONIA observations from January 1997 through December 2025, showing the pre-2009 cycle, the long low-rate period, the rise after 2021, and subsequent easing.", fig.cap="Monthly average SONIA, January 1997 to December 2025, from the verified official IADB replay."}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = date, y = value)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Monthly average SONIA, 1997–2025",
      subtitle = "Monthly published observations",
      x = "Month",
      y = "Rate (per cent)",
      caption = "Source: Bank of England IADB via readboe"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

With `format = "xml"`, the return value is a `boe_iadb` object: a named list
with `metadata` and `observations` data frames. The metadata keeps the official
series label, frequency, category fields, definitions, and comments. The
observations data frame includes `series_id`, `date`, the raw value columns,
numeric companion columns, provisional values, confidentiality markers,
revision timestamps, observation comments, and source row numbers. Dates are
`Date` values; missing or suppressed raw markers remain explicit.

`format = "csv"` provides the compatibility observation table; XML additionally
supports update filtering and observation footnotes. Both formats carry a
`boe_provenance` attribute on successful retrieval. That list records the
canonical and final URLs, retrieval time, raw byte count and SHA-256 hash,
HTTP validators when present, whether the response came from cache, the source
identity, transformations, and the package version. For a fresh bounded
request, use the visible `read_boe_series()` call; documentation rendering
uses the installed verified replay described below.

The replay contains 348 monthly observations from 31 January 1997 through
31 December 2025. Its 43,319-byte response was retrieved on 25 August 2026
with SHA-256
`3e1baa084a68d9e98e5ca01fabe3bf113c933f4e0cf530ebd99e7ac1b89ddfa0`.
The Bank [reformed SONIA on 23 April 2018](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/news/2018/april/sonia-interest-rate-benchmark-reform),
so compare the earlier and later portions with that methodology change in
mind. `readboe` preserves the observations under their official identity; it
does not splice or transform the series.
SONIA and/or SONIA Compounded Index data licensed under the Open Government
Licence v3.0 and copyright the Governor and Company of the Bank of England.
The trade marks “Bank of England” and “SONIA” are registered trade marks of
the Bank of England.

## Browse Bankstats and yield-curve files

Discovery of exact file identities is offline. Use the resulting URL as the
input to the corresponding reader so the package can preserve its identity and
provenance checks.

```{r file-registries}
bankstats <- boe_bankstats_assets(limit = 1L)
bankstats[, c("table_label", "url", "file_type", "archive", "member_count")]

yields <- boe_yield_assets()
yields[, c("asset_id", "scope", "curve", "frequency", "archive_revisable")]
```

`read_boe_bankstats()` returns named worksheet data frames and preserves the
worksheet cells and source coordinates while leaving header interpretation,
aggregation, NA dropping, and duplicate handling explicit for downstream code.
`read_boe_bankstats_series()` joins an exact series identity
to either its full canonical IADB history or the shorter current workbook
window. `read_boe_yield_curve()` returns a long data frame retaining raw and
numeric rate values and the source member, sheet, row, and column coordinates.
All three readers impose explicit byte, archive, workbook, and output bounds.

## Scope and limitations

The bundled catalogue covers the authenticated Bankstats page represented by
its manifest. A known official IADB identifier can also be requested directly.
The release-family registry is available offline; exact release-asset discovery
and reading become available after a verified pinned `release-assets.rds`
snapshot is supplied. Current-workbook readers represent the rolling workbook
window, while canonical IADB readers provide the full-history route. See the
troubleshooting article for typed failures and remediation paths.
